=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:879-911 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In alert_claims(), the guard `if match.group(2) != parking and match.group(2) != "overflow": continue` lets a trusted `parked=overflow` claim cover every later parking of the same item, and needs_human_prune never deletes claim comments, so a later parking with a fresh stamp returns `already_attempted` and never pages.
  WHY: The requirement is "at most one persisted CRITICAL alert attempt per needs-human parking", but after one overflow parking this becomes at most one attempt for the item's lifetime. Reviewers disagree on severity: google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rate it MAJOR with confidence 4; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rates it NIT with confidence 2 and calls it a scoped-out residual that fails in the documented direction (a lost page is preferred to a duplicate). minimax_minimax-m3 said this is by design and did not raise it. The highest rating (MAJOR, mapped to high) is used.
- tests/test_operator_step_issue.py:547-557 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: test_needs_human_alert_claim_skips_an_attempted_parking (lines 547-557) and test_needs_human_park_alert_skips_a_parking_already_attempted in tests/test_unblock_judge.py (lines 3037-3043) assert that a prior `parked=overflow` claim causes `already_attempted` for a fresh-stamp parking. This locks in once-per-item-lifetime semantics, and no test covers a fresh-stamp parking after an old overflow claim that must still page.
  WHY: Any fix that bounds overflow coverage by the claim's created_at would have to change these assertions, so the tests would block the repair.
- tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py, tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py, tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py, ruff, shellcheck:pre-push test gate results on head SHA 2967624d061f69f78215e9a180ef21c6ca2853b5 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The pre-push test gate blames this change for the `ruff`, `shellcheck`, `tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py`, `tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py` and `tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py` failures in two consecutive runs, and the last autofix run fixed none of them.
  WHY: The PR cannot merge while its own pre-push gate and the CI static checks fail. If the shellcheck finding is in the rewritten `if ! declare -F ...` blocks at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:22290 or scripts/unblock_judge.sh:212-218, the skip-path classification is also at risk.
- scripts/tg_helpers.sh:145 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The curl call in `tg_send_msg` has no `--max-time` limit.
  WHY: A hung Telegram endpoint would stall `unblock_needs_human_alert` / `needs_human_park_project` indefinitely while the claim stays at `state=attempted` and is never sent. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash raised the same point only as a hardening suggestion (HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:alert_claims(), `if match.group(2) != parking and match.group(2) != "overflow": continue` | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: A trusted `parked=overflow` claim covers every later parking of the same item, and claim comments stay on the item after needs_human_prune drops its digest entry. A re-parking with a fresh stamp, or a second overflow parking, therefore returns `already_attempted` and never pages.
  WHY: The requirement is one alert per parking, but this behaves as one alert per item. It only happens when the digest holds 200 or more entries. The reviewer records it as a scoped-out residual, because the P6b summary puts re-entry and the epoch reset out of scope, and the failure goes in the documented direction (a lost page is preferred to a duplicate).
- HARDENING: scripts/tg_helpers.sh tg_send_msg, the `curl -s -X POST "https://api.telegram.org/bot${TG_BOT_SECRET}/sendMessage"` call (around line 145)
  PROBLEM: The curl call has no `--max-time`, so a hung Telegram endpoint stalls the judge op loop or the poller tick while the claim stays at `state=attempted`. `tg_send_report_msg` already bounds its request.
  WHY: Suggested fix is to add `--max-time 30`. A timeout gives an empty message id, which the callers log as `outcome=unconfirmed reason=send_failed_or_ambiguous`. Estimated 1 line; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2.
- NOTE: TASK COMPLETENESS is NONE. The pass-1 TASK_GAP about `test_gh_api_write_guard.py` and the other CI failures does not hold up: no failing test covers files this PR changes, and the only failed check-run is copilot-pull-request-reviewer (`custom_instructions_too_large`, statusCode 422).
- NOTE: The reviewer checked and found correct: the `helper_missing` / `telegram_unconfigured` split, the parametrize-to-loop test rewrite, the `--slurp` fake branch (scripts/unblock_judge.sh line 167 uses `--paginate` without `--slurp`), and the `orchestrate_state_v2.py extract --require-latest` path. No tests were run, and the `login_unavailable` failures in tests/test_unblock_judge.py were neither confirmed nor ruled out. (4 related items)
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:alert_claims function, line 894 (docstring line 879) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `parked=overflow` claim comment is treated as covering every parking of the item forever.
  WHY: `alert_claims` keeps claim comments after `needs_human_prune` removes the digest entry, so a re-parking finds the old `parked=overflow` claim, returns `already_attempted`, and never alerts. This violates "at most one alert attempt per parking".
- scripts/tg_helpers.sh:`tg_send_msg` curl call at line 145 | severity=NIT | confidence=3

  WHY: A hung Telegram endpoint would stall `unblock_needs_human_alert` / `needs_human_park_project` indefinitely with the claim stuck at `state=attempted`, which can block the poller or judge tick.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:alert_claims(), lines 894-896 (`if match.group(2) != parking and match.group(2) != "overflow": continue`), with docstring lines 879-880; consumed by needs_human_alert_claim() at lines 908-911 and by both callers (scripts/unblock_judge.sh unblock_needs_human_alert, scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh needs_human_park_project via `needs-human alert-claim`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A trusted `parked=overflow` claim matches every future `--parking` argument of the item, and needs_human_prune never deletes claim comments. Every later parking (a real re-block weeks later, or a prune-promoted entry with a fresh stamp) therefore returns `reason=already_attempted`. The code cannot tell a promotion apart from an unrelated future parking.
  WHY: Example: the item is parked over cap at T0 and an overflow claim is recorded; a person unblocks it; it is re-parked with stamp T1; the old overflow claim matches; the judge or poller skips with already_attempted; and the operator is never paged for a parking that had zero attempts.
- tests/test_operator_step_issue.py:test_needs_human_alert_claim_skips_an_attempted_parking (lines 547-557) and test_needs_human_park_alert_skips_a_parking_already_attempted in tests/test_unblock_judge.py (lines 3037-3043) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new tests assert the unbounded overflow coverage as correct, which locks in once-per-item-lifetime semantics, and no test covers a fresh-stamp parking after an old overflow claim that must still page.
  WHY: A fix that bounds overflow coverage by the claim's created_at (a claim covers a parking only when the parking stamp is <= T_c) would require changing these assertions.
- tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py, tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py, tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py, plus `ruff` and `shellcheck`:pre-push test gate results on head SHA 2967624d061f69f78215e9a180ef21c6ca2853b5 (reported in the PR body for two consecutive runs); CI job `static-checks` still queued/in_progress | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The pre-push gate attributes these 5 failures to this change in two consecutive runs, and the last autofix run fixed none of them.
  WHY: The PR cannot merge while the gate and CI static checks fail. A shellcheck finding in the `if ! declare -F ...` blocks at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:22290 or scripts/unblock_judge.sh:212-218 would also put the skip-path classification at risk.
- HARDENING: scripts/tg_helpers.sh tg_send_msg, curl invocation (~line 145, pre-existing function newly called from the persisted-claim path)
  PROBLEM: The send curl has no `--max-time` (unlike tg_send_report_msg at ~line 177), so a hung endpoint stalls needs_human_park_project or unblock_needs_human_alert while the claim sits at state=attempted.
  WHY: Suggested fix is to add `--max-time 30` to match the report-send call. Estimated 1 line; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2.
